title: Chapter 85
content:
"Try calling her again. There's no way she'd just vanish."

Having barely dragged himself back from the brink of death, Wang Ryun seemed completely indifferent to the two brothers who had kept his heart beating, caring only about his missing girlfriend.

A few hours earlier, the tactical security detail had transferred him to Haewon's private VIP hospital—the very institution where Kang Yu-jung practiced as a senior physician. Ryun couldn't fathom why his lover wasn't answering her phone or rushing to his bedside, while Jakyeong and Han merely traded uneasy, tight-lipped glances, mumbling noncommittal excuses.

Given how fragile his recovery was, dropping the truth on him right now would trigger an absolute catastrophe.

To be thorough, Jakyeong had doubled back to the boutique hotel she was staying at, only to find the suite scrubbed completely empty. Afterward, he had cased Kim Dong-myung’s penthouse: the shattered glass, bullet-chewed drywall, and blood-soaked balcony were already impeccably repaired, freshly painted, and vacuumed clean, as if the midnight firefight had been a collective hallucination.

The efficiency was terrifying. In their world, snuffing out lives and vaporizing physical evidence overnight was standard operating procedure.

While they were brooding over the implications, a crisp knock sounded at the door.

The handle turned, and Kang Yu-jung stepped inside wearing a tailored white physician's coat, offering Jakyeong a warm, radiant smile.

Jakyeong quickly stood from the edge of the mattress, bowing his head. "Hello, ma'am."

"I heard you had a patient admitted," she said gently, moving over to review Wang Ryun’s medical charts and surgical drains. "If you’d brought him straight to my department from the start, I would have closed that wound with a far prettier stitch."

Beside the bed, Wang Han stood frozen, staring at her profile with a look of pure, unadulterated awe.

Once Yu-jung exchanged a few brief, clinical remarks with Jakyeong and excused herself, Han immediately pounced, whispering frantic questions about her identity. Discovering that the ethereal doctor was Kang Il-hyun’s biological sister left him in stunned disbelief.

"My god... Good looks must be an inherited disease in that family."

Han spent the next three minutes singing her praises, declaring he’d never witnessed a more angelic woman in his life, with Ryun nodding in enthusiastic agreement from the pillows. Jakyeong kept his mouth firmly shut. The last time his gaze had lingered on Kang Yu-jung for three seconds, Il-hyun had threatened to carve out his eyeballs and mount them in a silicone skull.

Not that he was afraid, of course. Just... cautious.

Before Han could compose another poetic verse regarding her beauty, another sharp knock interrupted them.

Three heads snapped toward the doorway.

Kang Il-hyun strolled into the room. Yet what seized the trio's attention wasn't the man himself, but the massive bouquet of pristine white chrysanthemums cradled in his arm.

Jakyeong’s brow pinched into an incredulous knot. What the hell is that? Wang Han wore an identical look of utter bewilderment.

Ignoring the room, Il-hyun immediately zeroed in on Jakyeong. He devoured him with a ravenous visual sweep from the messy dark bangs on his forehead down to his scuffed combat boots. Finding the boy standing relatively unharmed, a flicker of pure relief crossed his dark eyes—until his gaze drifted toward the bed, pausing on the bandaged man with a look of mild, genuine surprise.

"Ah. You're alive?"

Ryun scowled, only to let out a sharp, breathless hiss as the deep stab wound in his flank pulled taut.

Without a trace of ceremony, Il-hyun casually tossed the funeral bouquet into the plastic wastebin by the door. Having rushed back to Seoul the second he heard Jakyeong had been caught in an ambush, he had completely tuned out the operational debriefing regarding Wang Ryun’s status.

Assuming the man was already in the morgue, he had picked up traditional memorial flowers on the drive over. Since the corpse was breathing, the arrangement was useless.

Catching onto the sheer absurdity, Jakyeong stared in exasperation. "Did you seriously not even check whether he survived before buying flowers?"

Il-hyun smoothly adjusted his demeanor, flashing an innocent, apologetic smile. "The initial field report was scrambled. Don't be angry, darling. My sincere apologies, Mr. Wang Han."

Il-hyun addressed the wounded man on the bed as Wang Han.

A heavy, suffocating silence descended over the room as the three operatives realized that, to this very second, Kang Il-hyun still couldn't tell the two older brothers apart. Ryun looked emotionally shattered. After sharing expensive scotch and assuming they had forged an unspoken brotherly bond, discovering he was completely interchangeable in the CEO's eyes was a brutal blow to his pride.

Before Ryun could protest, Il-hyun’s phone chimed. He excused himself with a brief nod, stepping into the corridor to take the call.

The second the latch clicked, Ryun threw his head back against the pillow in disgust.

"Is that man even human? A guy nearly gets gutted on his payroll, and he walks in with funeral wreaths? As long as Wei is breathing, the rest of the world can rot, huh?"

"Now do you see?" Jakyeong agreed dryly. "I told you he wasn't cool. You're the one who wouldn't stop singing his praises."

Han shook his head in solemn disappointment. "I'm genuinely let down by President Kang. For a moment, I actually considered him a decent match for you."

Jakyeong bristled, snapping defensively. "A match for who?!"

Ignoring the bickering, Jakyeong noticed Il-hyun hadn't returned despite ten minutes having passed. He pushed off the wall and stepped into the hallway. Down near the end of the concourse, the man was pacing with a phone pressed to his ear.

Jakyeong took a seat on the vinyl bench outside the room, waiting.

Moments later, heavy, polished footsteps approached. Il-hyun paused before the bench, his eyes conducting another meticulous, head-to-toe inventory of Jakyeong’s condition—taking in the dried blood spattered across his tactical shirt, the unwashed hair, and the neat white gauze wrapped around his forearm.

"Finished with your call?"

"Yes. Corporate counsel," Il-hyun replied smoothly. "I had to abandon the Jeju negotiations midway the moment I heard you were hit."

"You should dock the pay of whoever gave you the report. Then you wouldn't have wasted money on funeral flowers."

Il-hyun let out a quiet chuckle. In truth, he was quite fond of white chrysanthemums—often considering having fresh arrangements placed throughout his estate, though the senior housekeeper had vehemently vetoed the idea as an ominous curse.

Meeting Il-hyun's dark, focused irises, Jakyeong averted his gaze, murmuring softly:

"I'm sorry... The operational leak came from our side. It won't happen again."

Il-hyun didn't offer a rebuke, his gaze remaining pinned to the bandage on the boy's arm.

"And you? Are you truly intact?"

"As you can see. Barely a scratch."

"Then that's all that matters. Don't go getting hurt anymore. An old fossil’s heart can only take so many frights."

Jakyeong scowled at the petty callback, yet beneath the irritation, a quiet, soothing warmth settled over his chest. It was unsettling. Throughout the grueling hours of Ryun’s surgery, the memory of Il-hyun's teasing, drawling baritone had relentlessly echoed in his mind. He had hovered over his contacts a dozen times, itching to call under the guise of an operational report—convinced that hearing that arrogant voice would drive away the suffocating panic.

Looking back, he couldn't explain the impulse. Had the relentless grooming actually worked? Have I genuinely developed feelings for this lunatic?

When the conversation tapered off, Il-hyun gently rested his heavy head against Jakyeong’s shoulder. Jakyeong didn't pull away.

In the quiet hum of the hospital corridor, Jakyeong broke the silence.

"I ran into Chairman Kang this morning. Outside the lobby."

"You should have put a bullet through his forehead." Il-hyun’s tone was entirely casual, yet his dark eyes sharpened into ice.

"He told me not to trust you. Said you'd be the first to cut my leash and let me bleed when things go sideways."

Il-hyun let out an amused, velvet chuckle, as if listening to a mediocre joke. "And what did you say to that?"

"Told him I never trusted you to begin with."

Il-hyun smiled, offering no counterargument.

Jakyeong hesitated, wrestling with the surveillance prints on his phone. Why had the man sent Park Tae-soo to meet Yoon Mi-ra with a duffel bag of cash? Even if he showed the evidence, would Il-hyun offer an honest answer?

In his head, the pendulum swung violently between trust and suspicion.

Do you know what became of the previous companions who shared President Kang’s bed?
Aren't you even mildly curious?
Whether they are walking among the living... or rotting under the dirt?

"Stop drowning in your own head," Il-hyun said softly, his cheek still resting against Jakyeong’s shoulder. "If you have a question, just ask."

Though tossed out casually, the man had read his internal turmoil with terrifying precision.

After a long beat, Jakyeong pulled out his phone, pulling up the photo of Tae-soo and the woman.

Il-hyun squinted at the screen, his eyes narrowing slightly. "Is that Tae-soo's girlfriend?"

Jakyeong gave him a look of utter exhaustion. "It's Ryun-ge’s lover."

"What? She's cheating on your brother with Park Tae-soo?"

This idiot is impossible.

"You genuinely don't remember?"

Il-hyun studied the screen for another second before letting out a soft, enlightened hum. "Ah... Right. Tae-soo tracked her down shortly after you fled the country."

"And?"

"She traded your brother's coordinates for cash. Which allowed us to take him hostage and drag you back to Seoul."

"You... paid her off?"

"Naturally."

"That was all?"

"What else was supposed to happen?"

Jakyeong stared down at the man leaning against his shoulder. Il-hyun lifted his head, his dark gaze locking onto Jakyeong's face with disarming clarity.

"I can read it in your eyes, darling. Half of you wants to believe me... and the other half is terrified to."

"..."

"I don't blame you. I did try to put you in the ground once, after all."

Feeling entirely exposed, Jakyeong looked away.

"When I gave the order to execute you back then... I meant it," Il-hyun murmured, his baritone steady and unvarnished.

Hearing the cold truth spoken aloud sent a sharp, bitter pang through Jakyeong's ribs. He clamped his jaw shut in silence.

Il-hyun rested his cheek back against Jakyeong’s shoulder, his voice dropping into a soft, quiet confession:

"And the fact that I'm crazy about you right now... is just as real."

"..."

"I'm late, but I apologize."

"..."

"I made the wrong call. If I’d known I would fall this hard for you... I never would have pulled such a stupid, reckless stunt."

Jakyeong’s heart thumped hard against his ribs, a violent, traitorous rhythm echoing in his throat. Terrified the man would hear it, he kept his jaw locked, staring resolutely at the floor tiles.

Il-hyun straightened his posture, meeting Jakyeong's lowered gaze.

"Now then. Your turn."

Jakyeong forced his eyes up. "My turn for what?"

"You could have kept those photos to yourself and nurtured your suspicions in the dark. Why show them to me?"

Those fathomless, obsidian eyes drilled straight into his soul. Jakyeong parted his lips, struggling for an anchor. He didn't trust this predator—not entirely. But...

"You told me not to trust you, but to trust your money," Jakyeong muttered defensively. "Since you're pouring an obscene fortune into my account... I decided to give you the benefit of the doubt."

The truth was that, despite everything, he wanted to believe in the man himself. Unable to lay his raw vulnerability bare, he hid behind the cold logic of finance.

A slow, triumphant smile spread across Il-hyun’s handsome lips. Reaching out, he pinched Jakyeong’s cheek with affectionate firmness. When Jakyeong swatted at the hand, Il-hyun gave the flesh a playful, twisting tug.

"Look at you... stubborn to the bitter end."

"That hurts!"

"Just admit that you've fallen for me, darling."

Jakyeong finally pried the fingers away, only for Il-hyun to hook a hand around the back of his neck, pulling him into a firm, lingering kiss on the mouth.

Jakyeong recoiled in flustered panic, shoving against the tailored chest. "Are you out of your mind?! Looking at my filthy, bloodstained face makes you want to kiss me?"

"You look magnificent to me, darling. Splattered with blood or not."

Catching the triage nurse at the end of the hall staring in wide-eyed shock, Jakyeong bolted to his feet, planting both hands on Il-hyun's back to shove him toward the elevators.

"You've seen me. Now get the hell out of here."

Il-hyun rose with a lingering, reluctant chuckle. "I have to leave anyway—matters in Jeju need settling. I only flew up to confirm you were in one piece."

"I know, so leave."

"Support units will arrive the moment I step out. Head back to the villa, wash up, and get some proper sleep. You look exhausted."

After surviving a rooftop ambush and pacing a surgical ward for hours, the exhaustion was undeniable. Jakyeong gave a quiet nod.

Il-hyun cupped his cheek one last time, turning down the corridor toward the elevators.

Jakyeong remained standing outside the room, tracking the retreating silhouette until the metal doors slid open.

Stepping inside, Il-hyun offered a teasing wave of his fingers. Jakyeong lifted his hand to wave back—only to freeze, catching himself. He dropped his arm instantly with a scowl, spinning on his heel to duck back into the room.

Through the closing elevator doors, Kang Il-hyun let out a loud, delighted laugh.

Ding.

The moment the doors sealed completely, the warmth vanished from his features. His expression flattened into an arctic, terrifying void.

Down in the private ground-floor lobby, Park Tae-soo was waiting by the exit.

"Where is my father?" Il-hyun asked, his voice dropping into a lethal, venomous rasp.

"He is currently holding court at the main family estate, sir."

They strode out to the armored sedan. Popping the trunk, Il-hyun reached inside, drawing a matte-black automatic sidearm from the hidden compartment and sliding it smoothly beneath his tailored jacket.

A dark, murderous malice flickered across his unblinking eyes.
